prompt_text: My AC needs repair in Houston. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but to give the best, specific recommendations I need your ZIP code (or neighborhood) and whether this is an emergency (no cooling right now, a leak, gas smell, etc.).

While you reply, here’s a short, practical plan and a few reputable companies that commonly serve Houston plus why you might call each type:

If you need an immediate fix
- Call a 24/7 emergency HVAC service. They’ll prioritize a same‑day technician. Ask whether the diagnostic fee is waived if they do the repair.

Reliable Houston options to consider (give me your ZIP and I’ll tailor and confirm local availability/phone numbers)
- John Moore Services — Houston-based, long-established, broad service (repairs, maintenance, emergency), good online reviews and maintenance plans.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (local franchise) — large network for fast dispatch, standardized training and warranties; good for emergency service.
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (Houston franchise) — often manufacturer‑authorized for major brands and helpful for diagnostic/replacement of complex systems.
- ABC Home & Commercial Services (Houston area) — full‑service with preventive plans and lifetime warranties on some installs.

Which to call based on your situation
- Quick repair / emergency: call a 24/7 local company (John Moore or ARS are good bets).
- Brand‑specific problem / warranty claim: call a company that’s authorized by your unit’s manufacturer.
- If you need a replacement: get 3 written estimates (one local reputable shop, one national/large franchise, one independent specialist).
- Ductless / mini‑split: call a ductless specialist (ask if they’re certified for the brand).

What to ask when you call (use this script)
- “Are you available today? What’s your earliest appointment?”
- “What is your diagnostic fee and will you waive it if you repair it?”
- “Are your technicians NATE‑certified or manufacturer‑trained?”
- “Do you carry insurance and can you email proof of insurance and license/registration?”
- “Do you provide written estimates and warranties for parts and labor? How long?”
- “If it’s a replacement, do you offer load calculations and a written scope of work?”

How I can help next
- Give me your ZIP code, the system type (central AC, heat pump, ductless, rooftop), how old the unit is (if known), and the symptom (no cool, short cycles, leak, smell). I’ll return 3–5 vetted, nearby companies with phone numbers, what they specialize in, and which one to call first for your issue.
